title: Annotatio VI §.IV open: Fathers seem to give Indigni partaking — via metonymy
pass_a_gloss: §. IV. Indeed the Fathers sometimes seem to opine that even the unworthy become partakers of Christ’s body, but that happens because the Fathers speak metonymically, not rarely naming the Sacrament of Christ’s body, or the bread of the Lord, Christ’s body — after Christ’s own example.
pass_b_english: §.IV: the Fathers sometimes seem to teach that even the unworthy partake Christ’s body.
That appearance comes from metonymy — they often call the sacrament or the Lord’s bread “Christ’s body,” following Christ’s own speech.
source_text: §. IV. Equidem videntur quandoque Patres opinari, etiam indignos corporis Christi fieri participes, sed id inde evenit, quòd metonymicè loquuntur Patres, Sacramentum corporis Christi, seu panem Domini, ad exemplum Christi ipsius, corpus Christi haud rarò nuncupantes.

lemmas.gloss: bread of the Lord … Christ’s body
